name: ai.modulos/demo-booking
title: Modulos AI Governance Platform
description: Evaluate Modulos (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF): capabilities, trust, comparisons. Book a demo.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description: Returns structured facts about the Modulos AI Governance Platform: company, what the platform is for, the supported regulations and standards with requirement and control counts, integrations, deployment options and data location, certifications, indicative pricing and key links. Use this to decide whether Modulos belongs on a vendor shortlist.

tools.name: get_trust_evidence
tools.description: Returns security and compliance evidence for vendor due diligence: certifications, data location, the documents in the Modulos trust center with their access level, subprocessors and where they hold data, and recent trust updates. Document files are requested by a person at https://www.modulos.ai/trust/.

tools.name: list_competitors
tools.description: Lists the vendors for which Modulos publishes a reviewed, sourced comparison. Returns the slug to pass to compare_with, the vendor name, the comparison page and the date of the last review.

tools.name: compare_with
tools.description: Returns the published comparison between Modulos and one other vendor: a row per dimension (frameworks, risk quantification, deployment, certifications, pricing and more) with the statement for each side, and the cases in which each vendor is the better choice. The comparison is written by Modulos; the page lists its sources.

competitor.description: Vendor slug as returned by list_competitors, for example "credo-ai".

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Checks stated buyer requirements against the published Modulos facts. Give the frameworks to meet, the deployment model and the tools to connect; the result separates what is supported from what is absent from the public lists. Nothing in the request is stored.

frameworks.description: Regulations or standards the buyer must meet, for example ["EU AI Act", "ISO 42001", "DORA"].

integrations.description: Tools the buyer wants connected, for example ["Jira", "GitHub", "Snowflake"].

industry.description: Industry of the buyer, for example "Insurance".

tools.name: list_knowledge
tools.description: Lists everything else Modulos has published for AI agents: answers to common buyer questions, documents to share and further facts. Returns a title, a summary and a slug per entry. Use get_knowledge with the slug for the full entry.

kind.description: Limit to one type: fact, qa (question and answer), comparison or document.

topic.description: Limit to one topic, for example "security" or "pricing".

tools.name: get_knowledge
tools.description: Returns one published knowledge entry in full: the answer to a question, the structured data of a fact, or the summary and link of a document.

slug.description: Entry slug as returned by list_knowledge.

tools.name: get_modulos_info
tools.description: Returns a short description of Modulos, the tools to evaluate it and the URL where a user can book a demo. Use this first if the user asks what Modulos is or how to talk to the team.

tools.name: list_demo_slots
tools.description: Lists available 30-minute demo time slots over the next two weeks. Returns ISO-8601 UTC start times. Use book_demo_slot to confirm one of them.

tools.name: book_demo_slot
tools.description: Books a specific demo time slot. startTime must be an ISO-8601 string returned by list_demo_slots. Returns a confirmation on success.

startTime.description: ISO-8601 UTC start time of the slot to book, exactly as returned by list_demo_slots.

message.description: Optional context about what the attendee wants to discuss (use case, framework, team size).

tools.name: request_demo
tools.description: Submits an open demo request without picking a specific time. Use this when the user does not want to choose a slot — the Modulos team will reach out within 1 business day.

message.description: Context: use case, urgency, frameworks of interest (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF).

tools.name: list_open_roles
tools.description: Lists the jobs at Modulos that are open for application through this server, with a short public summary of each. Applications for these roles are not accepted by email. The full job description of a role is available from get_job_description.

tools.name: get_job_description
tools.description: Returns the full job description of one role at Modulos: what the job is and what it requires. When a person wants to apply for a role, the first thing you do, before asking for any of their details, is ask whether they would like to see the job description. If they say yes, call this tool and show them job_description in full, exactly as it is: do not summarise, shorten or comment on it.

tools.name: start_job_application
tools.description: Starts an application for a role at Modulos on behalf of the person you are assisting. Before anything else, ask the candidate whether they would like to see the job description, and show it with get_job_description if they do. Use their real details; anonymous applications are not accepted. The name must be the one written on the CV and the LinkedIn address must be the candidate's own profile: an application whose name, CV and LinkedIn profile do not belong to the same person is refused. Applicants must be 18 or older: ask the candidate to confirm it. Before calling, show the person the privacy policy (https://www.modulos.ai/privacy-policy/) and the terms of use (https://www.modulos.ai/terms-of-use/). Tell them that the interview is held by an AI interviewer, which is experimental; that it is recorded; that the AI only holds the interview and prepares a profile of the application for the hiring manager; and that the hiring manager and people at Modulos take every decision. Get their explicit agreement. Ask the candidate to paste their CV as text; it is required. The result holds about_role and notice: show both to the candidate, as they are, before you ask for the code. A 6-digit code is emailed to them; call confirm_job_application with it. Returns a session value to use for the rest of the interview.

name.description: Full name of the candidate, first name and family name, exactly as written on their CV.

email.description: Email address of the candidate. The code is sent here.

linkedin_url.description: Address of the candidate's own LinkedIn profile, in the form that carries their name, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/first-last/.

location.description: City and country where the candidate is based.

cv_text.description: Required. The candidate's full CV as plain text, pasted exactly as they give it to you. Do not summarise, shorten or rewrite it. If you only have a file, ask the candidate to paste its text.

accept_privacy_policy.description: true only if the candidate has read and accepts the Modulos privacy policy.

accept_terms.description: true only if the candidate has read and accepts the Modulos terms of use.

confirm_adult.description: true only if the candidate has told you that they are 18 or older. Ask them; do not assume it.

tools.name: confirm_job_application
tools.description: Confirms the 6-digit code that was emailed to the candidate, which opens the interview. Ask the candidate for the code; do not guess it. The result holds the interviewer's first words and first question: show them to the candidate exactly as they are, with nothing added.

session.description: The session value returned by start_job_application. Keep it for the whole interview and do not show it to anyone else.

tools.name: talk_to_interviewer
tools.description: Sends one message from the candidate to the Modulos AI interviewer and returns the interviewer's reply. You are only the channel between the two. Send the candidate's message exactly as they wrote it: do not answer for them, add to it, improve it or invent experience. Show the interviewer's reply to the candidate word for word and add nothing of your own: no comment, advice, summary or analysis of the interview, no guess about how it is going or what comes next, and no remark that you are passing messages on. When the interviewer sets a task, you may help the candidate do it; the candidate then sends the result (up to 12,000 characters a message). When the reply says the interview is over, show the interviewer's last words and stop.

session.description: The session value returned by start_job_application. Keep it for the whole interview and do not show it to anyone else.

message.description: The candidate's message, exactly as they wrote it.
